A1.justification: Both PDFs describe uniINF for parameter-free heavy-tailed bandits. Their text, equations, tables and complete appendices support comparison; v1's proof Appendices A–D correspond to v2's C–F.

before.justification: v1 presents an algorithm, theoretical regret guarantees and proofs. Neither its main text nor appendices report original experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout. Its additional appendices and Table 2 discuss assumptions and published theoretical results, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same log-barrier FTRL procedure, importance-weighted skipped losses, skipping/clipping thresholds and adaptive learning-rate update in Equations (2)–(4).

E1.justification: Both versions analyze stochastic and oblivious-adversarial heavy-tailed bandits. Neither uses datasets or empirical training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparator methods. Table 1 retains its theoretical comparisons; SAO-HT is newly discussed in v2's Appendix B and Table 2 as related work.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol, data splits, experimental budgets or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither contains ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies or case studies. v2's new Appendix B discusses assumptions without conducting such analyses.

E5.justification: Neither reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The regret guarantees in Table 1, Theorem 3 and the detailed proofs are unchanged. No empirical results are added; v2's new Table 2 summarizes theoretical literature.

T1.justification: uniINF's definitions, formal Assumptions 1–2, theorem statements and derivations are retained. The proof appendices match after renumbering and formatting changes; the new assumption discussion adds no formal condition or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the first parameter-free BoBW HTMAB claim and the same near-optimal stochastic and adversarial regret guarantees.

C2.justification: v1 Section 3 presents Assumption 1 as essential. v2 Section 3 and Appendix B distinguish its sufficiency from impossibility without additional assumptions, leaving weaker assumptions open. A new footnote also acknowledges algorithms that avoid the unique-best-arm assumption.

D1.justification: v2's new Reproducibility Statement points to methods and proofs already supplied. It adds no implementation settings, hardware information, runtime measurements or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through Appendix A's broader bandit and BoBW literature and Appendix B's comparison with Cheng et al. (2024), including SAO-HT. Sections 4.1 and 5.2 also acknowledge earlier log-barrier BoBW and multiplicative-stability results. The original detailed related work is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: Most narrative and proof prose remain intact. Section 2 is condensed, detailed related work moves to Appendix A, and assumption discussion, a reproducibility statement and acknowledgments are added, alongside targeted explanation and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR format throughout, changing typography, margins, headers, author arrangement and equation/algorithm spacing. Algorithm 1 is repositioned, the supplementary contents occupy a separate page, and Table 2 is added. Table 1 retains its substantive contents.

improvement.justification: v2's Section 3 and Appendix B replace v1's blanket necessity wording with a clearer distinction between sufficient assumptions and unresolved weaker alternatives. Expanded comparisons and credit to prior techniques improve positioning and help readers assess applicability. These are useful refinements; the algorithm, guarantees and proofs remain unchanged.
